newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila for talks with another breakaway Moslem group.
newsitem.headline: Manila for talks with another breakaway Moslem group.

text.p: The Philippines will start preliminary peace talks next week with an important Moslem guerrilla group demanding autonomy on the island of Mindanao, the state-owned Philippine News Agency (PNA) said on Saturday.
PNA said a Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) panel will meet government representatives on Tuesday in Sultan Kudarat in Maguindanao, a largely Moslem province in Mindanao.

The MILF was formed as a breakaway group in the late 1970s of the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) which signed a separate peace deal with the government last October, ending a 24-year war for an MNLF-led Moslem self-rule in the south that killed 125,000 people.
Representatives from both the government and MILF met on Friday to set the "ground rules of the January 7 meeting," PNA said.

Military estimates put the MILF strength at between 6,000 and 8,000 compared to the MNLF strength of 16,000. But some army officers regard the MILF as more dangerous than the MNLF because of its hard-line stance.
Other factions, including the extremist Abu Sayyaf group which the military has blamed for a spate of bombings and kidnappings in the south, are believe to number only a few hundred.
